items.title: Starmer, Zelenskyy meet in Yerevan as UK seeks to join EU's Ukraine loan program

featured_image.name: UK to enter talks on joining European Union's £78bn loan for Ukraine -  Yahoo News Canada

items.description: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer arrived in Yerevan, Armenia, on Sunday ahead of the 8th European Political Community summit, where he is expected to press for the United Kingdom's participation in the European Union's €90 billion loan program for Ukraine. The move marks a further step in London's post-Brexit rapprochement with Brussels, driven by shared concerns over the war in Ukraine and shifting transatlantic dynamics under the Trump administration.

items.title: Cargo ship attacked near Strait of Hormuz as peace talks stall

featured_image.name: Cargo ship near Strait of Hormuz reports attack as Iran makes new peace proposal

items.description:
A bulk carrier near the Strait of Hormuz reported being attacked by multiple small craft on Sunday, according to the British military's United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center, marking at least the 24th attack in and around the vital waterway since the Iran war began in late February.[1][2]

The UKMTO said the northbound vessel was attacked 11 nautical miles west of Sirik, Iran, east of the strait, and that all crew were safe. No one immediately claimed responsibility for the incident, the first reported in the area since April 22. The threat level in the region remains classified as critical.[3][2]

items.title: Trump launches 'Project Freedom' to escort ships from Hormuz

featured_image.name: Trump says US Navy could escort ships through Strait of Hormuz

items.description: President Donald Trump announced on Sunday that the U.S. Navy will begin escorting neutral foreign vessels stranded in the Strait of Hormuz starting Monday morning under an initiative he called "Project Freedom," framing the operation as a humanitarian mission amid increasingly dire conditions for tens of thousands of sailors trapped in the Persian Gulf.

items.title: Three dead in hantavirus outbreak on Atlantic cruise ship

featured_image.name: CAPE VERDE-HEALTH-TOURISM

items.description: A hantavirus outbreak aboard a polar cruise ship sailing the Atlantic Ocean has killed at least three people and left a fourth in intensive care, prompting an international public health response led by the World Health Organization.

items.title: Iranian supertanker carrying $220M in oil slips past US blockade

featured_image.name: Iranian tankers challenging US by turning on transponders: Analyst

items.description: An Iranian supertanker loaded with more than 1.9 million barrels of crude oil has slipped past the United States naval blockade and reached Southeast Asian waters, according to maritime tracking firm TankerTrackers.com, in one of the most visible challenges yet to Washington's effort to choke off Tehran's oil exports.

items.title: Bulk carrier attacked near Strait of Hormuz amid IRGC buildup

featured_image.name: When will Strait of Hormuz be 'safe' for commercial shipping again?

items.description:
A bulk carrier came under attack near the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, the British military confirmed, the latest in a long series of strikes on commercial vessels navigating one of the world's most contested waterways since the outbreak of the U.S.-Iran war in late February.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), the British Royal Navy-led agency that monitors maritime security in the region, said it received a report of an incident involving a bulk carrier approximately 53 nautical miles northeast of Fujairah, United Arab Emirates. The vessel's master reported explosions near the ship's position, according to the advisory. The crew was reported safe, with no injuries, and the vessel proceeded to its next port of call under naval escort.[1][2]

items.title: Trump vows US troop cuts in Germany will go 'a lot further' than 5,000

featured_image.name: US to withdraw 5000 troops from Germany in next 6-12 months

items.description:
President Donald Trump said Saturday that the United States will reduce its military presence in Germany far beyond the 5,000-troop withdrawal announced a day earlier, escalating a confrontation with Berlin that has strained the transatlantic alliance.

"We're going to go way down. And we're going a lot further than 5,000," Trump told reporters in Florida, according to CNBC. He did not specify how many additional troops might be pulled out or offer a timeline.[1]

items.title: Trump says he's reviewing new Iranian proposal to end war

featured_image.name: Trump is reviewing Iran's new proposal to end war, but 'can't imagine that  it would be acceptable' | Fortune

items.description:
President Donald Trump said Saturday that he is evaluating a new proposal from Iran aimed at ending the conflict that began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28, offering a cautious signal that diplomacy may not be dead despite days of pessimism from the White House.

"I'll let you know about it later," Trump told reporters as he prepared to board Air Force One at Palm Beach International Airport, adding that aides were preparing to give him "the precise wording now."[1]

items.title: Zelenskyy flags 'specific activity' on Belarus border

featured_image.name: Zelensky visits troops at Belarus border as Russia reports gains

items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Saturday that Ukraine had detected "rather specific activity" along sections of its northern border with Belarus, raising fresh alarm about the prospect of a renewed threat from the north as the war with Russia grinds past its fourth year.

items.title: Iraqi supertanker appears to cross Strait of Hormuz amid near-standstill in traffic

featured_image.name: Why shadow tankers are the only ships still moving through the Strait of  Hormuz

items.description:
Ship-tracking data surfaced Saturday showing that a very large crude carrier hauling Iraqi oil from Basra appears to have successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz, one of the latest vessels to navigate a waterway that has been reduced to a fraction of its normal traffic since the US-Iran war began in late February.

The Comoros-flagged VLCC Kin A — also known as the Helga — reappeared on automated identification system screens off Duqm on the Omani coast on Saturday, according to Bloomberg, after going dark for more than three days. The vessel, a 299,000-deadweight-ton supertanker built in 2000, had loaded crude at Iraq's Basra offshore terminal after arriving there in late April. It is now en route to China.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Iran accuses US of nuclear treaty violations at NPT review conference

featured_image.name: Iran says US not complying with nuclear non-proliferation treaty

items.description: The 11th Review Conference of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons opened on April 27 at United Nations Headquarters in New York, with UN Secretary-General António Guterres delivering a stark warning that the global nuclear order is deteriorating at an alarming pace. The four-week conference, running through May 22, has quickly become a forum for sharp exchanges among member states over disarmament, enrichment rights, and the treaty's relevance in an era of emerging technologies.

items.title: Israeli strikes kill dozens in Lebanon despite ceasefire

featured_image.name: Israeli air strikes on Lebanon kill 41 people in 24-hours

items.description: Israeli airstrikes across southern Lebanon killed at least seven people on Saturday, as the military issued evacuation warnings for nine villages and continued operations it says target Hezbollah infrastructure — in what has become a pattern of escalating violence despite a ceasefire agreed upon on April 17.

items.title: Trump calls US Navy 'like pirates' enforcing Iran blockade

featured_image.name: Trump says US Navy acting 'like pirates' to carry out naval blockade of  Iranian ports | FMT

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Friday described the US Navy as acting "like pirates" in enforcing Washington's naval blockade of Iranian ports, a remark that drew attention even as the administration escalated economic pressure on Tehran.

"We took over the ship, we took over the cargo, we took over the oil. It's a very profitable business," Trump said Friday evening, according to Reuters, recounting a recent vessel seizure. "We're like pirates. We're sort of like pirates but we are not playing games."[1][2]

items.title: US warns EU allies of arms delivery delays as Iran war drains stockpiles

featured_image.name: US warns European allies including UK and Poland of arms shipment delays, FT  reports | Reuters

items.description:
The United States has warned European allies including the United Kingdom, Poland, Lithuania, and Estonia to expect prolonged delays in the delivery of American weapons systems, as the ongoing war with Iran rapidly depletes U.S. munitions stockpiles, the Financial Times reported on Friday.[1][2][3]

The warning, delivered through bilateral channels, marks an expansion of earlier alerts that had been limited to Baltic and Scandinavian nations. It underscores how deeply the two-month-old conflict is straining America's defense industrial base and unsettling NATO allies already on edge over Russia.

items.title: Iran demands six Arab states pay reparations over war

featured_image.name: Iran ambassador tells U.S. envoy Waltz to 'be polite' at UN meeting | Fox  News

items.description: Iran's ambassador to the United Nations has formally demanded that six Arab states be held legally accountable for their role in facilitating the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, calling their actions acts of aggression under international law.

items.title: US to shut Gaza ceasefire center as Trump plan stalls

featured_image.name: Israeli Minister Smotrich Calls for US-led Center for Gaza to Be ...

items.description: The Trump administration is set to shut down the Civil-Military Coordination Centre (CMCC), the U.S. military-run facility in southern Israel that served as the centerpiece of Washington's effort to oversee the Israel-Hamas ceasefire and coordinate humanitarian aid to Gaza, according to an exclusive report by Reuters  citing seven diplomats familiar with the centre's operations.[1]

items.title: Trump says he's 'not satisfied' with Iran's latest proposal

featured_image.name: Trump's madman diplomacy isn't working on Iran

items.description: President Donald Trump on Friday cast doubt on the prospect of reaching a deal with Iran, telling reporters at the White House that he was "not happy" with Tehran's latest negotiating proposal and warning he would "blast the hell out of them" if diplomacy fails.

items.title: Trump to raise tariffs on EU cars and trucks to 25%

featured_image.name: US president Trump threatens EU with 50 per cent tariffs from June

items.description: President Donald Trump announced Friday that he will increase tariffs on cars and trucks imported from the European Union to 25%, accusing the bloc of failing to comply with the trade deal struck last year at Turnberry, Scotland. The move threatens to upend transatlantic trade relations at a moment when the EU is already navigating tensions on multiple fronts.

items.title: Iran accelerates weapons recovery as ceasefire talks stall, NBC News reports

featured_image.name: Iran shares rare view inside underground bunker filled with drone fleet

items.description: Iran is exploiting its ceasefire with the United States to unearth missiles, drones, and other munitions that were either hidden underground before the war or buried beneath rubble from American and Israeli airstrikes, according to an NBC News report citing a U.S. official and two other sources familiar with the matter.[1][2]

items.title: Israel rushed Iron Beam laser system to UAE to counter Iran attacks

featured_image.name: Israel's new laser system goes active - Breaking Defense

items.description: Israel secretly deployed its newly operational Iron Beam laser air defense system to the United Arab Emirates to help counter Iran's sustained missile and drone bombardment, the Financial Times reported Thursday, in the latest revelation of deepening military cooperation between the two Abraham Accords partners.[1][2]
